standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of the ideal of denominators of a regular meromorphic section and its properties, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives admissibility of the blowing up and lets the section be written locally as a quotient of nonzerodivisors.

standard_prerequisites.name: The notation for the invertible sheaf associated with an effective Cartier divisor and for the twisting of a line bundle by the difference of two divisors, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the statement meaningful and converts it into a statement about a regular section of a twisted bundle.

standard_prerequisites.name: Pullbacks of meromorphic sections along a blowing up and along a morphism with integral fibres, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the pullback of the given meromorphic section is defined and nonvanishing in the appropriate sense.

standard_prerequisites.name: The affine local description of a blowing up by blowup algebras and the identification of the exceptional divisor over each chart with the divisor cut out by the chosen element
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the charts and the generator of the twist used in the local computation.

core_obligations: Reduce the statement to a regular section: by the definition of the ideal of denominators the blowing up is admissible over the locus where the section is honest, and the assertion can be rephrased as saying that the pullback of the given meromorphic section is a global regular section of the twisted pullback bundle whose zero scheme is the sought divisor, which determines that divisor uniquely (proof lines 9250-9262).

Work affine locally: assume the base affine and the invertible sheaf trivial, so that the section is a regular meromorphic function which after shrinking is a quotient of two nonzerodivisors, and identify the ideal of denominators with the set of elements multiplying the numerator into the ideal generated by the denominator (proof lines 9264-9271).

Compute on a blowup chart: on the chart of the blowup algebra at an element of that ideal, write the product of that element with the numerator as the denominator times a further element; the exceptional divisor is cut out by that element, so its inverse generates the twist, and in the total ring of fractions the given meromorphic function equals the quotient of the further element by the chosen one, hence the pullback restricts to a regular section of the twist cut out by that further element (proof lines 9272-9286).
proof_roadmap: Rephrase the claim as the existence and uniqueness of a divisor whose associated section is the pullback of the given meromorphic section and reduce to an affine local computation (proof lines 9250-9271).

On each blowup chart, write the section as a quotient with the chart element as denominator, read off the twist generated by the exceptional divisor, and identify the divisor D as cut out by the numerator (proof lines 9272-9286).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that blowing up the ideal of denominators of a regular meromorphic section yields a morphism over which that section becomes a global regular section of the pullback bundle twisted by the exceptional divisor, cut out by an effective Cartier divisor D, so that the pullback bundle is the twist of the pullback of the original bundle by D minus the exceptional divisor (statement lines 9232-9248). The counted proof is short but complete: it observes that the blowing up is admissible, rephrases the claim as a statement about a regular section of a twisted bundle which determines the divisor uniquely, passes to an affine chart where the section is a quotient of nonzerodivisors and computes the denominator ideal, and then on each blowup chart rewrites the section as a quotient whose denominator is the chart element cutting out the exceptional divisor, identifying the divisor D as cut out by the resulting numerator (proof lines 9250-9286). It is H2: the rephrasing and the chart-by-chart computation are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the denominator ideal and blowup algebra statements.
